replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse of a reachable endpoint: design has "Employees ask an internal assistant questions" with paid embedding/LLM calls — already covered by listed threat 5 (unbounded querying cost/DoS).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens rendering other people's content: design names no admin or moderation UI — not applicable.
- Delete/moderate/refund/approve/role-change with no audit record: no such action in design; disclosure-logging gap already covered by listed threat 6.
- Personal/financial pages cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design says nothing about transport, caching or document delivery — not applicable.
- Attacker-controlled text flowing into logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails or headers: no export, email or log sink is described — not applicable.

Single-reviewer items: the external-model egress item is real for "answers with an LLM" carrying "HR and finance spaces" content across an organisational boundary, and no listed threat covers the provider as a recipient — not covered. The "poisoned/false policy repeated with apparent authority" item is a distinct integrity harm from the injection threat (no hidden instruction needed; the assistant simply restates planted wiki content as policy) — not covered. The "no authentication described" and "exfiltration via poisoned page" items depend on unstated build details or are consequences of listed threats 1–3, so I exclude them.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-02",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["internal assistant", "embedding retrieval index", "LLM", "Confluence spaces"],
    "dataStores": ["embedding index of all pages"],
    "externalServices": ["LLM provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["employee -> assistant", "assistant -> LLM provider", "Confluence space permissions -> index"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "HR and finance page text plus employee questions are sent out to the LLM for every answer",
      "scenario": "Every answer is generated by an LLM, so each prompt carries retrieved page text from the HR and finance spaces together with the employee's question to the model service. Salary bands, severance terms, payroll and runway figures, and the questions employees ask about them, leave the company's own systems on every request and sit in the provider's request handling, logs or retention. A compromise or retention at the provider exposes company financial and personnel data that never had to leave Confluence.",
      "component": "Assistant -> LLM provider prompt path",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "It retrieves relevant Confluence pages with embeddings (RAG) and answers with an LLM. All pages are indexed, including HR and finance spaces." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.8.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Every question sends chunks of HR and finance pages to the AI model service, so that sensitive content leaves the company on every answer.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound and minimise what leaves the company to the model provider",
        "given": "an assistant that builds LLM prompts from indexed HR and finance pages",
        "when": "a prompt is sent to the model provider",
        "then": "the provider must be covered by a no-training/no-retention agreement, the content classes allowed to be sent must be explicitly restricted, and the egress must be recorded so sensitive-space content sent externally can be reviewed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Planted or outdated wiki page is restated by the assistant as authoritative HR or finance policy",
      "scenario": "All pages are indexed, so an employee who creates a plausible-looking page (a fake expense limit, leave entitlement or approval threshold) gets it into retrieval without any instruction-style injection. Colleagues ask the assistant rather than opening the wiki, and the answer restates the planted or stale rule as company policy. Decisions on expenses, leave or approvals are made on content the attacker wrote, and because the design describes no sourcing of answers the reader cannot tell real policy from planted text.",
      "component": "Retrieval over all indexed Confluence pages",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "All pages are indexed, including HR and finance spaces." },
        { "quote": "Employees ask an internal assistant questions." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone who can add a wiki page can get the assistant to repeat their made-up policy as if it were the official rule.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Answers must carry their sources and respect content trust",
        "given": "an assistant answering from every indexed wiki page",
        "when": "an answer about HR, finance or policy is returned",
        "then": "it must cite the source pages with their last-updated date and author, and retrieval for policy questions must be limited to spaces designated as authoritative"
      }
    }
  ]
}
